question: When a machine takes over a job's name and its routine tasks, does the work, and the people who do it, move on, and can the newest workers still find a way to start?

issues.note: Hard cut from the stylised 3D desk scene to a sepia archival photograph of two women and a man. The look changes completely with no transition.
The narration says 'the second kind of work', but the picture jumps from the 1950s office to an unexplained dark archive corridor. The shot has no clear link to what was just said.
Sepia photo of the IBM 704 room cuts straight to a 3D office of rows of desks. The change from photo to render is abrupt, and the narration 'check the machine's numbers' is only partly matched.
The picture goes dark and shows the office through glass reflections while the narration introduces 'two job titles'. It is murky and does not illustrate the point until the next shot.
The closing line 'the question this time' plays over a dark, dim street. The mood does not match a question being asked, and the lamplighter story has no payoff before the end card.
The 'Programming is one of many work activities…' quote card stays up across R10.6 to R10.8, about 12 s of text with nothing new to see.
The BLS handbook quote card holds across R09.5 and R09.6, about 8 s, as static text.
Frames R12.4 to R12.8 stay on the same dark office or screen with only numbers or captions changing, about 20 s.
The empty dark office shows in R14.5, R14.6 and R14.7 with only captions changing, about 12 s. It recurs in R13.5, R13.6 and R14.8 and R15.4 to R15.8.
Several near-identical dusk street frames across R16.5 to R16.8 and R17.1, about 20 s, before the end card. The camera does little.
